title: Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a priest, as related in the Yerushalmi, Berakhot, chapter 3, halakhah 1. When his father-in-law, who was also his teacher, died, he asked Rabbi Yosi whether he might become ritually impure for him, and Rabbi Yosi forbade it. Rabbi Acha heard and said that he might become impure (in Nazir, chapter 7, halakhah 1, the reading is Rabbi Chama). In [Yerushalmi Shabbat, chapter 6, halakhah 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.5.3), Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira’s ear ornaments fell from his ears on Shabbat. He wanted to put them back, but his colleagues rebuked him.[^1] In Taanit, chapter 2, halakhah 6, and at the beginning of Avodah Zarah, chapter 4, R' Yannai Ze’ira speaks in the name of his forebears. It is very likely that the R' Yannai found in the sequence ‘R. Z., R' Yannai, R' Yirmeyah’ in Shabbat, chapter 2, halakhah 3, is R' Yannai Ze’ira.[^2]
Mevo ha-Yerushalmi conjectures that he is R' Yannai son of R' Yannai Saba, mentioned at the end of Megillah.[^3]

notes.text: Hyman calls the objects הטרכין. The checked Guggenheimer edition of Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:5 describes Yannai Ze’ira’s ear object falling and his companions’ rebuke משום תכשיט, treating it as an ornament. This supports the general rendering ‘ear ornaments’; the precise kind remains uncertain, so ‘earrings’ is not asserted. The digital passage uses different wording, עודדיה דאודניה. The differing attributions to Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Chama elsewhere in this article are Hyman’s reported textual variant.

‘Very likely’ preserves the strength of Hyman’s identification; it is his argument, not an independently established identity. R. Z. represents the initials ר״ז, without deciding their expansion. ‘Forebears’ does not specify an individual father.

Mevo ha-Yerushalmi is treated as a title, without identifying its author or edition. The final genealogy remains explicitly that work’s conjecture. Hyman’s ‘end of Megillah’ does not specify Bavli or Yerushalmi; no additional locator is supplied. The opening account was also checked in Guggenheimer’s Berakhot 3:1:15 and Nazir 7:1:7, which explicitly write Rabbi Yannai Ze’ira, Rabbi Yosi, and respectively Rabbi Acha and Rabbi Chama. These checks support the titles at those occurrences; the later citations and Mevo ha-Yerushalmi conjecture remain unchecked.

R' preserves Hyman’s abbreviated titles in the later reporting and identification claims where a matching full-title occurrence was not checked. A full title from the ear-ornament account is not transferred to those other passages or to the conjectured father and son.
